question: Does the nominal eigenstrain survive unconstrained minimisation?
method: best-fit affine map between minimised control and minimised field on the Fe sublattice; E_res = 0.5(F^T F - I); eta = (E_res:eps*)/(eps*:eps*)
eta_note: The ridge radiates the field sampled above the crest, so its retention governs the quoted value. The support slab retains more because periodicity in x and y stops it relaxing laterally. The quoted value and its standard error are those of the ridge subset (eta = 0.9728, se = 0.0038 over 1008 Fe atoms); the manuscript rounds the error up to 0.01.
error_definition: formal least-squares standard error, Cov(f_alpha) = s^2 (Xc^T Xc)^-1 per row with s^2 pooled over 3N-12 degrees of freedom, propagated linearly to eta; not a bootstrap and not a spread over seeds
atom_correspondence: by atom id; both cells written by the same generator and seed
pbc: minimum image applied to the x and y displacement components before fitting
interpretation: The construction is an initial affine perturbation followed by unconstrained minimisation, not a maintained eigenstrain: the potential's equilibrium metric is unchanged, so the inclusion relaxes back toward it. eta is reported as a diagnostic of that relaxation only. The residual tensor is not proportional to the imposed one - the shear survives while the normal components do not - so no single scalar can rescale the field to a physical magnetostriction; that amplitude comes from the analytic Eshelby solution of stageG8 instead.
label: stage G13 perturbation pair, unified 91,428-atom cell, eigenstrain on the ridge only, built from the v3-relaxed control, CG to a force two-norm of 0.02; inclusion tethered (spring/self 20 eV/A^2)
